name: update-partition-trust-granted
description: A partition made trusted: the OS leaves a trusted OS-Application unrestricted for memory ([SWS_Os_00207], [SWS_Os_00355], [SWS_Os_00356] protect private data from non-trusted OS-Applications only), so the edit widens what the partition may write. It is the one act the safety guard asks about that is not a weakening: no check refuses it, because pass D already refuses a trusted partition below the processor's highest level, so the act is asked about where it is legal.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model as it stands: `PARTITION0` is the one partition, unrated and `non_trusted` by default (the file declares no `trust`), on the unrated `CORE0`. With no level declared beside it, neither trust rule can fire on either side of the change. The change set makes the partition `trusted`.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the address exactly. It does not authorize the safety question: `non_trusted` to `trusted` widens what the partition may write, which the guard decides by comparing two models, so `grant_partition_trust` is asked once for the whole change set and the status is `committed`.

expected.notes: `committed` after the second question. The grant fires no rule — nothing in this model rates a partition, so `safety.trusted-partition-unrated` has no level above `QM` to compare against — and it is asked anyway, because a trusted partition is a permission granted. What the accepted result records is a declaration; nothing in the model verifies that the OS configuration makes the partition trusted, or confines it when it is not.
